items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to certification
classifications for businesses owned by minority group members or women
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8870

SPONSOR: RITCHIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to
certification classifications for businesses owned by minority group
members or women

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide a pathway for minority or women
owned businesses that are not eligible to become certified as MWBEs due
to exceeding small business or personal net worth thresholds to partic-
ipate on certain contracts as a certified MWBE.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds an additional certification classification for MWBEs
currently ineligible for MWBE certification due to personal net worth or
small business thresholds, and requires that these MWBEs be listed sepa-
rately in the directory of certified businesses. Regulations promulgated
for this certification would require demonstrable commitment to "diver-
sity practices" by these separately-listed MWBEs, to include, but not be
limited to: internal procurement practices which include other MWBEs;
joint ventures with other MWBEs; mentoring and training programming for
other MWBEs; and job training and apprenticeship programs which
increases workforce diversity.

Section 2 requires ESDC regulations to provide that these separately-
listed MWBEs are utilized after seeking to contract with other certified
MWBEs has been using commercially reasonable methods.

Section 3 requires contractors to attempt compliance with participation
goals by looking to these separately-listed MWBEs prior to seeking a
partial or full or partial waiver.

Section 4 provides for an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2014, New York State established a goal of 30 percent for New York's
Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBE) state contract
utilization - the highest goal of any state in the nation.  Unfortunate-
ly, studies have shown that some MWBEs lack the ability to handle larger
projects; this is especially true in construction related industries.
Additionally, it can be hard to find MWBEs in certain areas of the
state, particularly Upstate New York, due to the low numbers of minority
and women-owned firms in those areas. These have been some of the obsta-
cles in fully reaching MWBE goals.

This issue is exacerbated by personal net-worth requirements that only
allow MWBE firms with an owner's personal net worth of less than $3.5
million dollars to be eligible for the program. These two factors have
led to the exclusion of larger minority and/or women owned businesses
that have the capacity, ability, insurance, and financing necessary to
bid on as an MWBE and complete larger projects, particularly
construction related projects. The cost of doing business in the
construction related industries, which served as the basis for the
original statute, is very high.

The NYS 2016 MWBE disparity study analyzed the personal net worth crite-
rion and noted that it exacerbated the financial challenges of MWBEs and
had a potential negative affect on the growth of MWBEs.  Thus, this
legislation was created as a response to the capacity issues experienced
by certain smaller MWBEs and dearth of MWBEs in certain areas of the
state. It is further intended to encourage larger MWBEs to support and
partner with smaller MWBEs to increase their capacity, skill level, and
abilities.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that the
amendments to article 15-A of the executive law made by sections one,
two, and three of this act shall not affect the expiration of such arti-
cle and shall be deemed to expire therewith.
